outcome: mode of delivery (cesarean section vs. vaginal)
cohort: Pregnant women admitted to the Department of Obstetrics and Gynecology of the Postgraduate Institute Yashwantrao Chavan Memorial Hospital, Pimpri, Pune, India, between April 2020 and April 2021, irrespective of gestational age or labor status, who were universally screened for COVID-19.
finding: There was insufficient evidence to suggest that cesarean section was superior to vaginal delivery in preventing COVID-19 transmission from mother to neonate.
mod_finding: The cesarean section rate among COVID-19 positive pregnant women was 31.59%, with higher maternal mortality (1.4% vs. 0.00%) and neonatal COVID-19 infection rates (0.46% vs. 0.22%) compared to vaginal delivery.
